# UI/UX Design Standards

## Principles

- Prioritize clarity, simplicity, usability, and consistency.
- Maintain a calm, modern visual style suitable for personal journaling.
- Prefer familiar interaction patterns over decorative complexity.
- Every visual element should serve a clear purpose.

## Layout & Spacing

- Maintain consistent page widths, alignment, and hierarchy.
- Use a predictable spacing system instead of arbitrary values.
- Group related content and clearly separate distinct sections.
- Preserve useful whitespace without wasting screen space.
- Adapt layouts intentionally for desktop, tablet, and mobile.

## Typography

- Maintain clear hierarchy between titles, headings, body text, labels, and supporting text.
- Keep equivalent typography roles consistent.
- Prioritize readability, especially for journal content.

## Color

- Use a restrained, consistent palette.
- Reserve accent colors for meaningful actions, moods, states, and emphasis.
- Use semantic colors consistently for success, warning, error, and destructive actions.
- Preserve hierarchy and readability in light and dark themes.
- Never rely on color alone to convey important information.

## Components & Interaction

- Equivalent components must look and behave consistently.
- Clearly distinguish primary, secondary, and destructive actions.
- Provide predictable loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, and success states.
- Keep interactive targets easy to identify and use.
- Require confirmation for destructive or irreversible actions.
- Avoid unnecessary motion or visual clutter.

## Accessibility

- Maintain readable contrast and legible text.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus.
- Use clear labels and meaningful feedback.
- Keep primary actions discoverable across screen sizes.
- Avoid horizontal scrolling and overcrowded controls.
